full_judgment:
3. The defendant Nos.3-5 contested the suit by filing written statements. The material case of these defendants was that Lynda Sundary, wife of Puma Chandra Chowdhury left this country before 20 years and consequently the suit land was taken over by the Government as per section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 "I. Because the learned trial court and the High Court Division fell into a serious error of law occasioning failure of justice in finding that the Ext-4 series (the sale deeds) are not genuine only because the plaintiff failed to examine the attesting witnesses of the deeds, whereas, the learned judge failed to consider the evidence of P.W 2 Sudhir Lal Shaha who categorically stated that 'জ্ঞানদা আমার ঠাকুর মা। শিব নাথ শাহা আমার জৈঠাতো ভাই । জগবন্ধু আমার জ্যেঠা। জগবন্ধু ও শিব নাথের লেখা আমি চিনি ।----- জ্ঞানা নাঃ সম্পত্তি নাঃ দলিল ৩টি অংশে বিক্রয় করিয়াছে। জ্ঞানদা এ সময় এদেশে ছিল। ----- নাঃ ক্রয় বিক্রুয় সম্পর্কে আমি জানি। ----” and as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside by this Hontble court. 

 15. Admittedly, the suit land has been recorded in S.A Khatian No. 19 in the name of Gyanda Sundari. But subsequently the suit land was taken over by the Government as per section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Since, the plaintiff has completely failed to prove that Gyanda. Sundari was living in this country around 1972-73, it can be assumed that Lynda. Sundary, wife of Puma Chandra. Chowdhury left this country. Apart from this the defendant proved the suit land had been used as pond by the public at large for more than 30/40 years at least. 

 16. Further as to the record of rights it is to be quoted profitably Section 144(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was inserted after Section 144 of the Act by East Pakistan ordinance VIII of 1967. Section 144A Provides: 

 17. If we glean the said provision it transpires that a finally published record of rights revised under Section 144(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has a presumption of correctness and that presumption continues till it is otherwise rebutted by reliable evidence. This proposition of law is well settled. In the case in hand since the R.S record has been prepared in the name of Government, the plaintiff could not produce any reliable evidence to controvert the same, so the submissions of the learned Advocate in this regard is a falacious one. 

 18. We have also found that excepting taking notice of contradictory statements court of appeal below did not controvert or reverse or set aside any finding of the trial court as regard possession or gen-ninety of Exhibit-4, but decreed the suit. Learned Judge also did not discuss the depositions of witnesses particularly 7 witnesses examined by the defendant. Possession is a question of fact and to find actual possession, oral evidence is required to be considered. It is the case of the Government that people at large use the pond which learned judge of the appellate court did not at all consider.
